item.title: Experts seek soil-based fertiliser recommendations to improve yields
item.description: By Cynthia Alo Agricultural experts have called for a shift from one-size-fits-all fertiliser recommendations to soil-based application, warning that farmers may be wasting money on nutrients their crops do not need. They said differences in soil conditions and crop requirements meant that applying the same fertiliser rates across farming locations could result in poor nutrient use, higher production costs and lower productivity. The experts spoke at the 2026 Nigeria Fertiliser Summit on Phosphorus and Food Security, organised by the Institute of Agricultural Research and Training (IAR&T), Obafemi Awolowo University and the Fertilizer Producers and Suppliers Association of Nigeria (FEPSAN), with the Fertilizer and Inputs Support Services Department of the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security as co-convener in Abuja. Findings presented at the summit by the Regional Hub for Fertilizer and Soil Health for West Africa and the Sahel showed that phosphorus requirements for maize and rice in northern Nigeria ranged from zero to more than 60 kilogrammes of phosphorus pentoxide per hectare, depending on soil conditions. Phosphorus is an essential plant nutrient that supports root development, crop growth and grain formation. However, its availability to crops varies with soil properties and farming conditions. A soil scientist and modelling expert at IAR&T, Prof. Vincent Aduramigba-Modupe, said improving agricultural productivity required more than increasing fertiliser application. “Improving crop productivity is not only about applying fertiliser. It is about ensuring the right nutrient is applied in the right amount, at the right place, and under the right conditions,” he said. The Minister of Agriculture and Food Security, Aliyu Abdullahi, represented by the Director of Agricultural Land and Climate Change Management Services, Oshadiya Olanipekun, emphasised soil data, testing and crop-specific fertiliser recommendations as important tools for improving farmers’ outcomes. Also speaking, Prof. Jibrin Mohammed Jibrin, Visiting Scientist with the Regional Hub and Professor of Soil Science at Bayero University, Kano, described soil information as fundamental to food production. Jibrin also called for better coordination among agricultural stakeholders, warning that fragmented interventions could undermine efforts to improve soil health. “The basis of food production and food security is the soil. You need healthy soil to produce well and feed the nation with nutritious food. To do that, you need soil intelligence. “Too many initiatives have been implemented in silos. Real progress will come when stakeholders align, collaborate and follow through on agreed actions,” he said. Senior Agronomist at the Regional Hub, Dr. Bello Shehu, said improving phosphorus management was not about applying more fertiliser but understanding the nutrient requirements of different soils and crops. item.title: Ogun indigenes reaffirm support for Adebutu ahead of 2027
item.description: …PDP candidate’s supporters pledge grassroots mobilisation for ‘Ogun for Ogun’ agenda By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta Indigenes of Ogun State have reaffirmed their support for the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate, Oladipupo Adebutu, and his running mate, Yemi Sowunmi-Kolapo, pledging grassroots mobilisation for their ambition ahead of the 2027 governorship election. The pledge was made during ward-to-ward engagements by the candidates across local government areas of the state, where residents expressed concerns about poor infrastructure, unemployment, inadequate agricultural support and the need for improved access to modern farming equipment. The campaign tour is also aimed at presenting the candidates’ seven-point development agenda, tagged ITURA DE, to the electorate. At the ward meetings, community leaders, market women, farmers and youths turned out to receive the candidates and discuss their expectations from the next administration. Several stakeholders pledged support for the ‘Ogun for Ogun’ initiative, arguing that the state’s leadership should reflect the interests, heritage and aspirations of its indigenes. At Alagada Ward in Obafemi Owode Local Government Area, a market leader, Mrs Folasade Ogunye, said her support for the movement was informed by the belief that indigenous leadership would better understand the challenges confronting grassroots communities. She lamented the poor condition of roads leading to markets and the limited employment opportunities available to young people, pledging to mobilise women for door-to-door campaigns. “We, the women of Obafemi Owode, have suffered neglect. Our roads to the markets are bad, and our children need jobs. We want someone who grew up here, who knows our language and understands our struggles,” she said. At Alapakooni community, also in Obafemi Owode, some residents said to be former members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) publicly renounced their membership of the party. The defectors reportedly set bunches of APC brooms ablaze to symbolise their departure, citing dissatisfaction with the party’s political leadership and questions surrounding the identity of its governorship candidate. A community youth coordinator, Tunde Akinola, said their decision to align with Adebutu was motivated by their desire for leadership they could identify with and hold accountable. He said the group wanted to support a candidate who understood the state’s challenges and could deliver on his promises. Similarly, a community stakeholder and farmer at Onidunu Ward, Deji Bamidele, said farmers in the area wanted a government that would prioritise agricultural development through mechanisation and improved access to farming inputs. He said a farmers’ cooperative with more than 300 members had pledged support for the ‘Ogun for Ogun’ initiative, following Adebutu’s presentation of his agricultural plans under the ITURA DE agenda. item.title: 2027: I’m on a mission to rescue Abia South — Ikonne
item.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — The All Progressives Congress (APC) senatorial candidate for Abia South in the 2027 general election, Prince Paul Ikonne, has pledged to attract federal projects and employment opportunities to the zone if elected. Ikonne made the pledge while addressing members of the Catholic Women Organisation (CWO) at Christ the King Cathedral, Aba Diocese, where he described his candidacy as a mission to rescue the zone and accelerate its development. He alleged that Abia South had suffered poor representation over the past 20 years, resulting in inadequate federal presence, infrastructure and empowerment opportunities. The candidate promised to attract federal projects to the zone, facilitate federal employment for youths and secure agricultural and business grants for artisans, market women and entrepreneurs. He also pledged to ensure that Aba, which he described as the commercial hub of the South-East, received its share of federal infrastructure. Ikonne urged residents to support his ambition, saying his proposed representation would be focused on delivering measurable benefits to the constituency. “Enough is enough. For 20 years, we have had representation without results, or projects, and leadership without impact. It is time to change that narrative. “My representation will be vocal, visible and valuable. I will not be a Senator in Abuja without impact to my constituency while my people suffer. We will move from excuses to progress, from lamentation to legislation,” he said. He called on members of the CWO to mobilise voters in support of his candidacy, describing women as an important grassroots political constituency capable of influencing electoral outcomes. Ikonne also commended the organisation for its contributions to family life, the growth of the Catholic faith and community development. In separate remarks, the CWO President in Aba Diocese, Lady Nneoma Florita Ngozi Anwuacha, and some parish presidents commended the candidate for what they described as his support for the diocese. They assured him of the organisation’s support in the 2027 election, citing his association with the church. item.title: Reductionism and the national question: restructuring or grievance? (I), by Usman Sarki
item.description: “The co-existence of several nations under the same State is a test, as well as the best security, of its freedom. ” — Lord Acton Nigeria’s convoluted debate on restructuring has endured for decades because it supposedly speaks to questions of power, identity, representation, resource distribution, security, federalism and belonging. Precisely because the debate has been driven largely by sectional advocates and habitual agitators, however, it has also become increasingly burdened and polarised by a tendency towards reductionism, or the habit of explaining the country’s many and complex difficulties through a single grievance, a single historical narrative, a single ethnic experience or a single constitutional remedy. It is here that the discourse on the so-called “national question” becomes difficult, protracted and, at times, almost futile. Nigeria undoubtedly has structural problems, just as other countries do. It also has governance challenges, adversarial politics, elite misconduct, civic indiscipline, institutional weakness, manufactured discontents and problems arising from deep historical memories. To collapse all these into one argument that Nigeria will work better only if one particular restructuring formula is adopted may be emotionally satisfying, but it is intellectually shallow and politically reactionary. The central question, therefore, is no longer simply whether Nigeria should restructure. It is whether restructuring is being presented as a panacea, pursued as a genuine national project, or increasingly deployed as an instrument of demagoguery, a mockery of democracy and a vocabulary through which competing groups selfishly articulate accumulated grievances. That distinction is essential if an honest national discourse is to be undertaken. A federation is, by its nature, an arrangement for managing diversity. It seeks to reconcile unity with autonomy, common citizenship with regional identity, and national authority with sub-national self-government. Nigeria’s problem is not that diversity exists; that is an enduring fact. The more difficult question is whether the state has developed institutions capable of managing that diversity fairly, equitably, peacefully and productively. Lord Acton’s dictum is instructive in this regard. The coexistence of several nations within one state is not necessarily evidence of political failure. It is, rather, a test of liberty and constitutional maturity. The challenge is whether institutions can make diversity compatible with freedom, equality and political order. When those institutions are compromised and rendered incapable of delivering satisfactory governance, every disagreement acquires an ethnic or sectional interpretation. Administrative failures become evidence of domination. Economic inequalities are interpreted as deliberate marginalisation. Political defeat is transformed into collective humiliation. item.title: Igbo youth rebuff of Nigerian Army (III), by Ochereome Nnanna
item.description: The purpose of this series is to explain why the young people of Igbo extraction now reject the offer to join the Nigerian Army. In the first part, we saw how the Army that Igbo senior officers once led with distinction became the instrument for their subjugation, both during and long after the Biafra War, despite promises to the contrary. In the second part, we also saw how the military, as a political force, was used to prevent the Igbo resumption of their pride of place, not only in the political power arena but also in virtually every sector of Nigeria’s affairs. Each time the Igbo are poised to lead the country, the Establishment uses the Nigerian Army to stop them in preference for less-fancied options, which is why the country is dying, not growing. The straw that finally broke the camel’s back was the return of Muhammadu Buhari in 2015 as an elected president. Ndi Igbo had wholeheartedly thrown their support behind Dr Goodluck Jonathan in the 2011 presidential election. Jonathan obtained victory despite withering opposition from the North and South West, and he identified Ndi Igbo as the great, avuncular force behind his victory. He appointed Igbo sons and daughters into commanding positions in his government, giving them posts that had always been denied them by the military and its civilian agents. These included Secretary to the Government of the Federation. Jonathan even mandated Ndi Igbo to nominate a candidate of their choice. He also brought back Dr Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala to serve as Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister for the Economy. She commanded the power of a virtual Prime Minister and helped build the Nigerian economy to emerge as the largest in Africa in 2014 after a strategic rebasing, with a GDP value of $509.9bn. By contrast, our economy has currently slid to the third position, behind South Africa and Egypt, with a GDP value of $386.67bn, according to many authoritative sources, including Business Insider Africa. It was also during that era that Nigeria stood on the threshold of defeating Boko Haram, with the Nigerian Army under the supreme command of Igbo-born Chief of Army Staff, Lt-Gen Azubuike Ihejirika. The North and South West plotted the defeat of Jonathan in his re-election bid in 2015. Ndi Igbo felt the pain of Jonathan’s loss as if he were their ethnic kinsman. They were also made to pay for their support of him by the new All Progressives Congress (APC), whose candidate, Muhammadu Buhari, emerged victorious. Glowing in his victory, Buhari went to America, apparently to thank President Barack Obama for his support after three previous failures. At the US Institute of Peace on 25th July 2015 in Washington, DC, Buhari uttered a grossly irresponsible undertaking: that he would give his supporters 97 per cent and only 5 per cent to those who did not support him. item.title: AI as election bogey, by Okoh Aihe
item.description: As he walked across the stage to address the gathering, the young MC joked on Monday morning that Prof. Joash Amupitan is one man nobody would really want to envy in Nigeria today. This was beyond a joke, which the INEC Chairman soaked in with some equanimity. In less than three months, his agency, which has struggled with a bout of image concerns, would be organizing some major elections which may give him a redeeming opportunity to change the calculus, to convince Nigerians that he can write a good story from a previously bad plot. It was the reason Amupitan was at the Continental Hotel in Abuja. Offered a platform at the National Summit on Electoral Information Integrity, jointly organized by the International Press Centre (IPC), the Centre for Media and Society (CEMESO) and DAI, with support from the European Union, he delivered a deeply troubling paper which could be summarized as follows: the fear of artificial intelligence (AI) is the beginning of good elections. “Today, elections can be undermined long before the first ballot is cast. The threat is no longer limited to physical interference (such as violent ballot snatching) at the polling unit; it takes shape within digital networks through synthetic media, automated misinformation/disinformation, deepfake fabrications, digital micro-targeting, and Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference (FIMI). The troubling reality is that many democracies are not really prepared for these,” Amupitan said. Addressing the Summit theme, Beyond the Ballot: AI, FIMI, and the Integrity of Nigeria’s 2027 Elections, Amupitan gave no room for fear but instead displayed a commanding grasp of the electoral ecosystem to rally stakeholders to the realization that the democratization of AI has unleashed more challenges for electoral managers to handle. We can help Amupitan tell his story from there. There was already AI in February 2023. But it was a computer glitch from the backend of the INEC setup that blemished the integrity of a national election which had gone well until that unfortunate intrusion. The exponential growth in AI technology, which even the promoters are beginning to be afraid of as they fear it can imperil life and other human activities, is creating a cluster of concerns globally, with Amupitan now having to call on the concerted efforts of stakeholders to rescue the 2027 elections from a technology which carries so much good and evil. Unfortunately for all of us, there are so many tech mavericks, the troubled cyber denizens who will always want to take advantage of the negative side of technology to create and extend damage just to satisfy their satanic instincts. This explains why the INEC boss alerted that the rapid democratisation of generative AI models has dramatically lowered the barrier to entry for malicious minds. item.title: Sanwo-Olu: One week and the different faces of a single development challenge
item.description: By DAVID OWENS There was a common thread running through several of Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu’s engagements in the last week of October: the future of Lagos and the resources required to build it. It was not immediately obvious from the variety of events he attended. Indeed, anyone following the governor’s activities from Monday, October 26, to Saturday, October 31, might have been struck first by their diversity. There was an economic summit, a women’s conference, an international business gathering, meetings with development partners, a political manifesto unveiling, a medical centenary, an education award ceremony, a bankers’ investiture and a fashion show. Yet, beneath the differences in setting and audience, several of these engagements raised essentially the same questions. How does Lagos attract investment? How does it translate infrastructure development into economic opportunity? How can public policy improve the conditions under which businesses and individuals operate? And how can a government prepare its institutions for the demands of a rapidly expanding metropolis? These were among the questions that gave coherence to an otherwise unusually crowded week. At the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit in Abuja on Monday, Sanwo-Olu approached Nigeria’s economic challenges from the standpoint of regional integration and trade. His contribution centred on the opportunities offered by the African Continental Free Trade Area, the importance of functioning trade corridors and the infrastructure necessary to facilitate commerce. For Lagos, these were not abstract economic propositions. A state with major ports, extensive commercial activity and growing industrial corridors has a direct interest in the efficiency of national transport infrastructure and cross-border trade. Sanwo-Olu argued that better roads, railways, electricity, broadband connectivity and logistics systems were essential to improving competitiveness. The significance of that position becomes clearer when considered alongside his activities two days later. At the Nigerian-British Chamber of Commerce executive business breakfast in Lekki on Wednesday, the governor returned to the subject of investment, this time with the future of Lagos itself as the centrepiece. The gathering, themed The Future of Lagos: Business, Investment and Global Competitiveness, brought him into direct conversation with investors and private-sector operators. He spoke about the state’s long-term development plan, the expansion of rail transportation through the Blue and Red Lines, infrastructure improvements and the movement of certain government services onto digital platforms. These investments, he argued, formed part of the foundation for a more competitive economy. But the discussion also illustrated the distance between ambition and implementation. item.title: Ramping up solar option to close energy gap
item.description: Nigeria’s electricity crisis indicts decades of failed planning. For a population approaching 240 million, the national grid remains unreliable, while millions lack access altogether. The World Bank’s access series put electricity access at 62.5 per cent in 2024; the Nigerian Investment Promotion Commission (NIPC) says more than 85 million people remain without grid power. Installed capacity guarantees nothing when gas shortages, transmission bottlenecks and distribution failures keep power from consumers. Successive administrations have promised relief through independent power projects, yet spending has delivered too little amid corruption allegations and poor accountability. Mambilla is the glaring cautionary tale. Conceived decades ago as a 3,050-megawatt hydroelectric project, it remains stalled by contractual disputes and litigation. In September 2026, an international tribunal rejected Sunrise Power’s claims against Nigeria and found settlement arrangements tainted by corruption. That ruling only removed a legal obstacle without switching on a single megawatt. Solar offers a practical route to closing the gap. Nigeria receives average solar irradiation of about 5.5 kilowatt-hours per square metre daily and has a theoretical potential of 427 gigawatts, yet uses less than two per cent of it. Rooftop systems, mini-grids and solar home systems can reach off-grid communities, power clinics and schools, and help businesses escape costly generators. Solar with batteries cannot meet every round-the-clock industrial need, but it can complement hydro, gas and a reformed national grid. President Bola Tinubu’s N10 billion solar project at Aso Rock, completed for testing in late 2025, is expected to reduce the Villa’s dependence on the grid. It demonstrates solar energy’s value and also the privilege gap: the Presidency is shielding itself from outages endured by ordinary Nigerians. The same determination must reach homes, markets, farms and public institutions. Government should scale up the $750 million World Bank-backed DARES programme, provide affordable credit and pay-for-service plans, and prioritise solar mini-grids in underserved communities. States can use the Electricity Act 2023 to license intrastate markets, attract private developers and solarise hospitals, schools, water systems and industrial clusters. Federal agencies should set transparent targets, stable incentives and guarantees that attract investment. India’s rooftop and agricultural solar programmes, alongside domestic panel manufacturing, show how finance, public procurement and clear standards can build markets. Nigeria should expand local panel assembly, then develop batteries, inverters, mounting structures and recycling through joint ventures and technology transfer. item.title: Indigenous tech solution targets fish losses with data driven farming
item.description: By Cynthia Alo High feed costs, fish mortality and inefficient water management are reducing the profitability of fish farming in Nigeria, prompting calls for wider adoption of technology that can help farmers improve production and cut losses. One such innovation is Smart Pond, developed by Pysis Technologies, an agritech startup using Internet of Things (IoT) technology and artificial intelligence to help fish farmers make production decisions based on actual pond conditions rather than assumptions. The technology monitors pond conditions and provides information to guide feeding and water management, addressing practices that often result in excessive feed use, poor water quality and avoidable fish deaths. Chief Executive Officer and Co-founder of Pysis Technologies, Oluwatoyin Ogundeji, said fish farmers still rely largely on assumptions to determine when to feed their fish or change pond water, leading to unnecessary production costs. He said: “Feed is already expensive, yet we still see about 15 to 20 per cent feed wastage, largely because farmers feed fish when their metabolism is low without knowing.” According to Ogundeji, farmers using the solution could reduce fish mortality by up to 89 per cent, while operating costs can reduce by as much as 10 per cent. He added that assessment of some farmers using the technology recorded profit margins of up to 55 per cent, compared with the 20 to 25 per cent he identified as the average for smallholder and mid-scale farmers. The device has a built-in aerator that supplies oxygen to pond water, allowing farmers to extend the period between water changes and reduce energy costs associated with pumping and replacing water. However, Ogundeji said the adoption of aquaculture technology also depends on addressing institutional challenges, particularly the policy classification of inland freshwater fish farming. He called for a review of the policy that moved inland freshwater aquaculture from the Ministry of Agriculture to the Ministry of Blue Economy, stressing that the change has made it difficult for aquaculture-focused agritech businesses to access some agricultural interventions and support programmes. According to him, more than 80 per cent of Nigerian fish farming takes place on land through freshwater ponds and tanks, making the subsector closely linked to agriculture through its dependence on land, agricultural feed inputs and local food production. He noted that while marine capture fisheries and offshore mariculture fall under the Blue Economy, inland freshwater aquaculture should remain connected to agricultural policies and support systems. To address farmers’ concerns about adopting unfamiliar technology, Pysis said it conducts demonstrations and refresher training through its Thriving Aquaculture Africa initiative. item.title: Ministry presents Zamfara budget performance report
item.description: The Zamfara State Ministry of Finance has presented the 2025 Budget Performance Report, highlighting how funds were utilised in the year under review. The Commissioner for Finance, Muhammad Bello Auta, presented the report during the 2025 budget performance and accountability meeting held at the Finance Ministry Multipurpose Hall in Gusau. Represented by the State Accountant General, Ali Akilu Muhammad Bungudu, the commissioner said that the 2025 Zamfara State Budget, tagged “Rescue Budget 2.0,” was approved at a total of N546,014,575,000. He said the budget was designed to focus on key sectors, including security, education, healthcare and agriculture, among others. Mr Auta maintained that approximately 72% of the total budget was allocated to capital expenditure, while about 28% was earmarked for recurrent expenditure. He also said that the report captured the amount of revenue generated from various sources and the amount spent from the approved budgetary allocations. He further explained that the ministries, departments and agencies that received funds, projects and programmes implemented with the allocated funds, and the level of implementation of major projects were all contained in the 2025 budget report. The commissioner also said that in line with the government’s efforts to promote transparency and accountability in the management of public funds, the Q4 2025 Budget Performance Report was published on 28th January 2026, providing important information for assessing the implementation and performance of the 2025 budget at the end of the fiscal year. He enumerated the projects and programmes identified by the government as beneficiaries of the 2025 budget, including the Gusau International Airport, Gusau-Magami-Dansadau Road, school projects, a modern medical research centre, Smart City, food production initiatives, hospitals, the Gusau International Conference Centre, the Gusau International Sports Centre, as well as road projects across various local government areas, adding that there was an important distinction between what was provided for in the budget and what was actually spent or implemented. item.title: Zamfara monarchs harp on sustained prayer for peace
item.description: The Emir of Gusau, Abdulkadir Ibrahim Bello, has called for constant prayers for the sustenance of peace and stability in Zamfara and Nigeria. He made the call in Gusau on Sunday at the grand ceremony organised by the emirate to honour the emir after receiving a Staff of Office and official recognition as traditional ruler from Governor Dauda Lawal. During the event, district heads, council members of the emirate, community and religious leaders from the emirate, with their subjects, paid homage and solidarity visits to the Emir over his coronation and receiving the Staff of Office from Governor Dauda Lawal. The emir urged the people of the emirate to avoid committing sinful acts that could attract the wrath of God. He called on the people to always fear God and devote themselves to praying to Almighty Allah to address the security challenges in the state. “My message to you is that you should always be law-abiding and live peacefully with one another for the development of peace and economic growth,” the Emir said. He commended Governor Dauda Lawal for his kind gesture and honour to the traditional institution. Meanwhile, the Emir of Birnin Yandoto in Zamfara, Alhaji Aliya Garba-Marafa, tasked his subjects on unity and peaceful coexistence. In a statement issued in Gusau on Sunday by the Chairman, Publicity Committee of the emirate, Nasiru Biyabiki, the monarch made the call while addressing his subjects in Yandoto after receiving the Staff of Office from Governor Dauda Lawal. According to the statement, the event was attended by district heads, council members of the emirate, religious and community leaders, among other stakeholders from within and outside the emirate. He also urged community leaders and district heads in the emirate to maintain peace, foster unity and avoid acts of injustice. item.title: Sultan is a beacon of unity and stability – Governor Lawal
item.description: Governor Dauda Lawal of Zamfara State described the Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar III, as a humble leader who brings people together and provides stability. On Monday, the governor attended the 13th Shaikh Usmanu Bin Fodiyo Week and the 20th anniversary of the coronation of Sultan Sa’ad, at the International Conference Centre in Sokoto. This year’s ceremony, with the theme ‘Reviving Ethical Leadership and Social Harmony: Lessons from Sokoto Jihad Leaders’, brought together notable figures from Nigeria and beyond. In his goodwill message, Governor Lawal said the government and people of Zamfara State have been greatly inspired by the Sultan’s wisdom, guidance, and steady leadership, especially during difficult social and security times. He said, “With immense joy, respect, and gratitude to Almighty Allah (SWT), on behalf of the government and people of Zamfara State, I congratulate His Eminence Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar III, 20th Sultan of Sokoto and leader of the Ummah, on the historic 20th anniversary of his coronation. “We remain deeply grateful for your recent presence and support at our coronation and presentation of staff of office to our 19 Emirs in Gusau, which further underscores your commitment to strengthening the traditional institutions across our region. “This year’s celebration reminds us that the Sokoto Caliphate’s legacy transcends borders. Its enduring values, knowledge, justice, moral discipline, responsible leadership and human dignity remain relevant to today’s challenges. “Closer to home in Zamfara State, this legacy carries a particularly compelling message. At a time when insecurity, moral decline, poverty and youth vulnerability threaten our communities, we must draw inspiration from the teachings of Sheikh Usmanu Dan Fodiyo to promote peace, justice, education and social responsibility.” Earlier, the Sultan thanked everyone who played a part and contributed during his 20 years as Sultan of Sokoto. He encouraged religious, traditional, and community leaders to work even harder to promote peace. item.title: Ekiti chiefs pledge one million votes for Tinubu in 2027
item.description: By Rotimi Ojomoyela ADO-EKITI – The Association of Ekiti Traditional Chieftaincy Title Holders has pledged to mobilise one million votes for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in the 2027 presidential election. The association made the pledge at a gathering hosted by the Managing Director of the Federal Housing Authority (FHA), Hon. Oyetunde Ojo, where traditional title holders from across Ekiti State expressed support for Tinubu’s administration and called for sustained implementation of its policies. The Chairman of the association, Chief Oluwole Ogunsakin, said the one-million-vote target represented its commitment to mobilising communities across the state ahead of the election. He said the association’s network extended to towns, villages, families and grassroots organisations, adding that members would encourage eligible voters to participate peacefully and freely in the electoral process. Ogunsakin also identified insecurity as one of the major concerns confronting residents, saying traditional rulers and chiefs were strategically positioned to contribute to grassroots security because of their closeness to the people. He welcomed ongoing legislative discussions on the establishment of state police, expressing optimism that the proposal would eventually become law. The association urged the government to consider involving traditional chiefs in screening and recommending credible candidates from their communities for recruitment into the proposed state police structure. Ogunsakin said such involvement would strengthen public confidence in the security system, given traditional leaders’ knowledge of their communities and local security challenges, including activities around farmlands. He said: “As custodians of our heritage and respected community leaders, we recognise the importance of peaceful democratic participation and constructive political engagement. “On this occasion, the Association of Ekiti Traditional Chieftaincy Title Holders declares its commitment and aspiration to mobilise one million votes through our communities in support of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election, while supporting your political mobilisation efforts. “We shall encourage eligible voters to participate peacefully and make their choices freely at the ballot box.” Speaking at the event, Ojo described the Tinubu administration’s infrastructure projects, particularly road construction, as unprecedented, comparing their scale to infrastructure development during the administration of former Head of State, General Yakubu Gowon. He said the roads being constructed under Tinubu’s administration were designed to last between 30 and 40 years. Ojo also commended the President’s appointments, saying they reflected fairness and representation across the country’s ethnic groups. item.title: Security: Traditional rulers critical partners – Lawal
item.description: Governor Dauda Lawal said the traditional institution is an important partner in promoting peace, stability, and development. The governor revealed this at the weekend when he presented staff of office and official vehicles to 19 emirs in Zamfara State. The coronation and presentation ceremony took place at the Trade Fair Complex in Gusau, the state capital. Among the dignitaries in attendance were the Sultan of Sokoto, the Etsu Nupe, and the Emir of Gwandu. Following their oaths of office, Governor Lawal presented staff of office to 11 first class emirs and eight second class emirs. Each newly coronated emir also received a GAC ULTRA SUV (2025/2026 model), a MIKANO ZNA HILUX vehicle, and an EV ANTIQUE MODEL car (DDP). The vehicles are intended to support their travels and help them engage more closely with their communities. In his remarks, Governor Lawal said the ceremony reflected his administration’s recognition of the traditional institution as an enduring part of society and an important partner in promoting peace, stability, and development. He noted that the ceremony also reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to giving traditional rulers the recognition and institutional support they need to carry out their responsibilities effectively. item.title: Abia: How one woman ended Okuenyi mothers’ dangerous trek for childbirth
item.description: …Govt promises standard facility By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — For pregnant women in Okuenyi community, Obingwa Local Government Area of Abia State, the journey to motherhood was often a painful test of endurance, one that began long before labour pains set in. With no functional health facility to attend to them, expectant mothers had to trek approximately three miles to neighbouring communities in search of antenatal care and safe delivery. For some, the journey was a desperate race against time, with the lives of both mother and child hanging in the balance. But one woman who grew up in the community could no longer bear the sight of her people enduring such hardship. Moved by the plight of the women, Mrs Ebere Ulelu-Obiesie, an indigene of Okuenyi, stepped in to change the narrative, sponsoring the renovation and upgrading of the community’s dilapidated temporary health post and equipping it with essential medical facilities. Her intervention, complemented by financial support from Rev. Friday Nnah, Proprietor of Abundant Living Christian School, Okuenyi, has brought renewed hope to a community whose women had for years faced the agonising prospect of travelling miles to access basic healthcare. For the women of Okuenyi, the renovated facility which was inaugurated recently, represents much more than refurbished walls and newly acquired medical equipment. It offers the possibility of receiving medical attention closer to home and, perhaps, a safer journey into motherhood. Painful reality that inspired intervention Narrating the circumstances that prompted the intervention, Mrs. Ulelu-Obiesie told SEV that her attachment to Okuenyi, where she was born and raised before marriage, made it impossible for her to turn her back on the suffering of her people. She disclosed that the decision to rehabilitate the health post was driven by her worry over the deplorable condition of the facility and the difficulties pregnant women in the area pass through to access healthcare. According to her, a visit to the health post with her husband, Mr Ernest Obiesie, exposed the gravity of the situation and strengthened her resolve to intervene. “I was born in Okuenyi before I got married. I could not stand by and watch my people continue to face these difficult challenges, especially in accessing healthcare services. Pregnant women, in particular, were exposed to enormous difficulties. “After visiting the former health post in Okuenyi with my husband and seeing its deplorable condition, I resolved to liberate my people from these challenges by initiating the project through my husband, in collaboration with my co-sponsors,” she said. Her husband, Ernest, revealed that he initially hesitated when she presented the proposal, citing financial constraints. However, seeing the condition of the health post during a subsequent visit changed his perspective, as the couple resolved to respond to the community’s urgent healthcare needs. item.title: Inter End Champions League Slump With 3-0 Win Over Feyenoord
item.description: Inter Milan got their stuttering Champions League campaign back on track with a comfortable 3-0 win Tuesday against Dutch giants Feyenoord, helped by a superb first-half strike from German defender Yann Bisseck. The three-time champions of Europe had lost their first two group games, but had far too much quality for a disappointing Feyenoord, who had little answer to Inter’s pace and attacking ability. On a clear and crisp evening in Rotterdam, the visitors quickly silenced the ever raucous crowd in De Kuip, piling on sustained pressure that paid dividends as early as the eighth minute. Bisseck was given too much space on the edge of the box, allowed to turn and drill a sumptuous curling left-footed shot low past the diving Tjark Ernst in the Feyenoord goal. Feyenoord struggled to break out of the Inter Milan high press and the Serie A champions dominated possession and territory for much of the first quarter. The home fans had to wait for half an hour before their side produced their first effort of note, a clever one-two playing in Anis Hadj Moussa, who saw his shot blocked. And Inter doubled their advantage shortly afterwards. Feyenoord’s Dutch midfielder #10 Luciano Valente (R) reacts at the end of the the UEFA Champions League, league phase, Matchday 4, football match between Feyenoord and Inter Milan at De Kuip Stadium in Rotterdam on November 3, 2026. (Photo by JOHN THYS / AFP) England international Djed Spence found himself in acres of space on the right hand side. His shot looped up off a defender, allowing Pio Esposito to bundle in with his head from short range. The beginning of the second half brought more misery for Giovanni van Bronckhorst’s men, as Feyenoord’s defence backed off and invited an advancing Piotr Zielinski to shoot. The Polish international midfielder gratefully accepted the invitation, firing home an unstoppable drive off the post on 54 minutes. With the game effectively over as a contest, Inter boss Cristian Chivu rang the changes, bringing off star striker Marcus Thuram. Halfway through the second half, fireworks launched from outside the stadium landed on the pitch and roof, causing a short interruption. And the match itself rather fizzled out, as Inter cruised and Feyenoord failed to find any spark to penetrate the Italian defences. The win saw Inter climb to a more respectable place in the middle of the Champions League table while Feyenoord’s solitary victory leaves them adrift of the knock-out phase. Feyenoord’s next Champions League encounter is a home tie against Porto, while Inter Milan welcome Stuttgart. item.title: Raphinha, Yamal Fire Barcelona To Champions League Win Over Villa
item.description: Raphinha struck twice to propel Barcelona to a 3-0 Champions League win over visitors Aston Villa on Tuesday, ending the English side’s perfect start to the competition. Five-time winners Barcelona took an early lead through Lamine Yamal before Raphinha continued his fine goalscoring form with a second-half brace. Barca bounced back after defeat by champions Paris Saint-Germain in their previous European outing to stay in the hunt for a top eight league phase berth. Unai Emery’s Villa competed well in the first half but were eventually undone by Barca’s greater ability in the final third. The Champions League anthem was not played before the game, as a mark of respect for Tenerife striker Jesus De Miguel, who died on Tuesday morning after an on-pitch collision in a Spanish second division match the previous day, provoking shock across the football world. Villa captain John McGinn had only visited the Camp Nou once previously, on a summer holiday as an eight-year-old, and might have expected better weather than the downpour both teams were subjected to. The skipper might also have expected a more focused start, with Villa handing Barcelona the lead in the seventh minute. Barcelona’s Spanish forward #10 Lamine Yamal (R) and Barcelona’s English forward #17 Anthony Gordon fight for the ball with Aston Villa’s Dutch defender #22 Ian Maatsen (L) and Aston Villa’s Swedish defender #03 Victor Lindelof during the UEFA Champions League 1st round day 4 football match between FC Barcelona and Aston Villa at Camp Nou Stadium in Barcelona on November 3, 2026. (Photo by MANAURE QUINTERO / AFP) The Spanish champions pressed Aston Villa extremely high and Joao Gomes played a poor pass straight to Yamal in his own box. The 19-year-old winger gladly took the gift and stroked past Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki. Villa reacted strongly and Matty Cash had a vicious drive deflected narrowly wide before Joao Cancelo blocked Gomes’s effort. Barcelona goalkeeper Joan Garcia was quick off his line to beat Nicolas Jackson to a dangerous through-ball. Suzuki saved from Anthony Gordon as Villa again struggled to bring the ball out from the back under Barca’s pressing. Garcia was called into action again by Johan Manzambi as the match lurched from end-to-end. Barcelona extended their lead early in the second half when Fermin Lopez fed Raphinha, who showed quick footwork before finding the bottom corner. Cancelo powered a strike narrowly over before setting up Raphinha for Barcelona’s third with a superb cross with the outside of his boot. The Brazil winger, who has made the number nine position his own this season, pounced from close range for his 19th goal of the season across all competitions. Yamal sent a shot skidding wide as Barcelona probed for a fourth. It did not come, but the Catalan giants were able to record a first Champions League clean sheet in 19 games. item.title: Atiku Alleges Plot To Disrupt ADC Campaign In Sokoto, Vows Resistance
item.description: Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has accused the Sokoto State Government and security operatives of working to frustrate the African Democratic Congress (ADC) campaign in the state, alleging that protesters were being mobilised to disrupt the party’s planned rally. Atiku, the ADC presidential candidate, made the allegations at a news conference in Abuja on Tuesday, claiming that the party had been denied access to public facilities and logistical support ahead of the rally. He said the restrictions were part of a deliberate effort to place the opposition at a disadvantage and undermine the right of Nigerians to freely choose their leaders. “These are not harmless administrative delays. They are deliberate attempts to deny the ADC a level playing field,” he said. ﻿ Atiku also alleged that the Department of State Services (DSS) was recruiting protesters to cause disturbances and create a situation that could be used to impose a curfew and prevent the rally from taking place. He identified an office behind Zenith Bank on Koko Road as one of the locations where the protesters were allegedly gathered. “We know where some of these protesters are assembled: an office behind Zenith Bank on Koko road. “Trucks are stationed there and dispatched to key points, including the roundabout. These mobilised protesters are causing gridlock. “Commuters are being threatened and, in some cases, beaten. Some of the protesters have moved away from the roundabout to find shade,” he said. The former Vice President accused security personnel allegedly involved in the operation of abandoning their professional duties for political interests. “This is not intelligence work. It is political interference dressed in official uniform. Security agencies exist to protect Nigerians and uphold the law, not to recruit protesters or help a political party manufacture a crisis,” he said. He asked the officers involved to end the alleged mobilisation and discharge their duties without political bias. Turning to the wider political climate, Atiku accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of attempting to weaken opposition parties by drawing their members into the ruling APC. He described the strategy as one of political absorption and intimidation, warning that its ultimate objective was to leave Nigeria with little meaningful opposition. “The aim is to reduce Nigeria to a one-party state in all but name,” he said. Atiku also faulted the Federal Government’s handling of the economy, pointing to the rising prices of food, transport, fuel and electricity as evidence of the pressure on households. He said the ADC would pursue policies aimed at expanding local production, increasing food supply, generating employment and lowering the cost of doing business if elected in 2027. Among his proposals is a targeted production subsidy linked to fuel refined in Nigeria. He said the measure would ease the burden on consumers while supporting domestic industry. item.title: Seen And Heard At The US Midterm Elections
item.description: Reporters, photographers and video journalists are deployed by AFP across the United States to document the 2026 midterm elections as Americans head to the polls. Here is a round-up of interviews on Tuesday at polling stations where voters agreed to share their thoughts about what was on their minds and motivating their choices. Hopeful Democrats With polling data suggesting the Democratic Party is on track to capture a majority in the House of Representatives and perhaps even in the Senate, many left-leaning voters said they were hopeful about the results. “Two years ago was a really devastating outcome for me,” Emma Mondadori, a 39-year-old who works in philanthropy, told AFP in Brooklyn, New York, referring to President Donald Trump’s election. “I’ve been really looking forward to this day where we get to have a say again in the future of our country… I’m cautiously hopeful, optimistic.” AUSTIN, TEXAS – NOVEMBER 03: Voters wait in line to cast their ballots at the polling place at the Baker Center on November 03, 2026 in Austin, Texas. Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images/AFP (Photo by CHIP SOMODEVILLA / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) The cost of living With gasoline prices up by a third since last year and diesel nearly double — not to mention sharp food price inflation — everyday spending was on many people’s minds. “It’s about the cost of living, gas prices, those kind of things. It needs to change for the everyday person, and I’m an everyday person,” Donta Comer, a 38-year-old project manager in Atlanta, Georgia, told AFP. Tom, a 27-year-old businessman at the same polling station who declined to give his surname, agreed. “Everyone, at least in my generation, is a little frustrated with the affordability crisis and gas prices and what’s going on abroad,” added the non-partisan voter. Leadership referendum Mid-term elections are typically seen as a form of referendum on the sitting president. And few leaders have polarized public opinion as strongly as Donald Trump. “I’m independent but I voted Democrat, I just wanted to go back into the culture of decency, integrity, honesty, and the rest follows,” Yan Cardineau, 59, told AFP in Austin, Texas. “If we lose that, it doesn’t matter how much money you make.” Atlantans head to the polls to vote on Election Day at Park Tavern on November 3, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. Megan Varner/Getty Images/AFP (Photo by Megan Varner / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) Estrella Roque, a 69-year-old voter of Cuban origin, told AFP in Miami she had voted Republican. “What I like about the Republicans is that they can fix the country,” she explained in Spanish. “Donald Trump hasn’t been given time to show who he really is.” Immigration In his final pitch to voters, Trump has stressed his success in reducing immigration and stopping crossings along the southern border with Mexico.
